offers_products.reason: Main offerings are lift access, lodging, dining, ski school; retail and rental gear are secondary to the resort experience.

offers_services.reason: Operates 42 mountain resorts selling Epic Passes, lift tickets, ski school, lodging, dining and rentals as experiences.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Skiers and riders buy Epic Passes, lift tickets, lessons, lodging and rentals.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Customers are individual skiers and families; no meaningful organizational buyers named.

recurring_revenue.reason: Revenue is mostly seasonal pass and ticket purchases; annual pass renewals are repeat, but guests choose yearly, so judged not ongoing.

cyclical_demand.reason: Luxury ski travel, lift tickets, lodging and lessons are discretionary and easily cut in downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Typical purchase is a lift ticket, lesson, meal or season pass; small-to-moderate and frequent relative to major purchases.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for access to owned mountains, lifts and lodging assets rather than mainly staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main customers are individual skiers and households, not large enterprises or government.

asset_heavy.reason: Owns and operates 42 resorts with lifts, lodging and facilities needing ongoing capital investment in new lifts and terrain.

notes: Recurring revenue is a close call: Epic Pass renewals are repeat purchases but sold annually, with seasonal ticket sales too.
